subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Present Bias and Hyperbolic Discounting
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Present Bias and Hyperbolic Discounting.

hook.text: Would you rather have $100 today or $110 tomorrow? Most pick today. $100 in 30 days vs $110 in 31? Most wait.

buildup.text: Present bias: we overvalue immediate rewards relative to future ones. The nearer the reward, the more it dominates.

discovery.text: Hyperbolic discounting means our discount rate isn't constant. We're patient about the distant future and impatient.

twist.text: This is why January gym memberships spike and February attendance drops. Future-self made a plan.

climax.text: Pre-commit when you're patient. Automate savings, schedule workouts, and remove the decision from your impatient.

punchline.text: Your patient future self needs protection from your impatient present self.

quiz.question: What does present bias cause?
options: Equal valuation of present and future rewards
Overvaluing immediate rewards relative to future ones
Preferring future rewards over present ones
